title: tk: per-file learnings budgets (head 4096, body 16384, 800 per body entry)
description:
In internal/tick/learnings.go and internal/tick/learnings_test.go; the warning call sites in cmd/tk/cmd/status.go and cmd/tk/cmd/close.go; and one line in CHANGELOG.md under [Unreleased] (Changed).

Behaviour:
- A head `.tick/learnings.md` over 4096 bytes warns, naming the file.
- A body `.tick/learnings-ref.md` over 16384 bytes warns, and a body entry over 800 bytes warns with its line number (reuse the existing entry parsing).
- An absent body gives no warning, and an absent head stays silent.
- Warnings never block. `tk status` and `tk close` print them per file.
- Keep the existing exported names working, or update every caller.

Use TDD with a planted fault: these are boundary and absent-file logic, the case where watching a test fail earns its cost.

This tick runs alone in its own worktree. Another chain is editing skills/ticks/ docs in parallel; do not touch them. Go is reachable only as `mise exec go@1.24 -- go …` (see .tick/learnings.md).

Shared vocabulary (verbatim across all three parallel chains, which do not see each other):
- Files: `.tick/learnings.md` is the always-read head (at most 4096 bytes: hard rules plus an index of the body's categories). `.tick/learnings-ref.md` is the looked-up body (Problem/Cause/Rule entries, at most 16384 bytes, at most 800 bytes per entry). The 800-byte entry limit applies to the body only. The engine owns the format; the project owns the content.
- Check labels in implementer reports: the tick-gate command verbatim, `by-path run`, `planted fault`.
- Check outcomes: `ran clean`, `went red and changed the code`, `went red, not from this change`, `not applicable`.
- Terms: "parallel warm-chains", "warm turn", "retire" (an implementer is retired after the final review).
- Existing section titles in agent-runner.md stay as they are. The gate names are "tick gate" and "wave gate", already defined.
Spec (source of truth): docs/thoughts/2026-11-12-lean-epics.md. Edit only skills/ticks/ (never an installed copy) unless your task names other files. Keep the engine's terse voice; criteria, not step lists.
acceptance_criteria:
- Named tests pass under `mise exec go@1.24 -- go test -short -count=1 ./internal/tick/ ./cmd/tk/...`. They cover the head boundary (4096 ok, 4097 warns), the body boundary (16384 / 16385), the body entry limit (800 / 801), and an absent body (no warning).
- `mise exec go@1.24 -- go build ./...` and `mise exec go@1.24 -- go vet ./internal/tick/ ./cmd/tk/...` are clean
- Each warning string names its own file
